claim: For the real plane \(X_w=d_*(1,w)^2\), \(0<w<1\), with \(\|(x,y)\|_w=\max\{|x|,|y|,(|x|+|y|)/(1+w)\}\), the Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_w,\ell_2^2)=\sqrt{2(1+w^2)}/(1+w)\) for \(0<w\le \sqrt2-1\), and \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X_w,\ell_2^2)=\sqrt{1+w^2}\) for \(\sqrt2-1\le w<1\). It is uniquely minimized at \(w=\sqrt2-1\), where it equals \(\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\).
integrity: The lower bound ranges over arbitrary ellipses via positive-definite quadratic forms, and the matching upper bound is explicit. Search absence is not treated as proof of novelty; the residual indexing risk is stated separately.
scientific_limitations: The proof is complete for the stated real two-dimensional family and all 0<w<1. The originality comparison has a notation/indexing residual: an older convex-geometry treatment of the same square--diamond octagon could exist without Lorentz-space terminology.
title: Exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance for a Lorentz-predual octagonal plane
